$comment: CMS-0057-F acceptance scenario manifest — the machine-readable SOURCE OF TRUTH for scenario status. The acceptance suite validates its [Trait("Scenario",...)] against this file (see ScenarioManifestTests), and tools/Cms0057Evidence generates versioned evidence from it. Statuses are one of: PASSABLE, PARTIAL, GAP, N/A. 'replace' is Cloud Health Office product capability (Replace mode). 'augment' is external-core integration capability (per backend). Do not invent Facets/HealthEdge results until an integration exists.

capabilityDefinitions.PASSABLE: The repository's defined acceptance scenario is supported by the tested implementation. Not a CMS certification and not by itself production readiness for a specific payer deployment.
capabilityDefinitions.PARTIAL: Core of the scenario is implemented; some part is engagement or roadmap work.
capabilityDefinitions.GAP: Not implemented in the tested code; tracked so it is not silently claimed.
capabilityDefinitions.N/A: The scenario has no dependency on this backend/dimension.

qnxt.rationale: QNXT benefit/auth-required lookup is per-engagement integration work; product path runs on the CHO rule store.
QNXT AUTH_CREATE is per-engagement integration work; product path persists via ChoAuthorizationBackend.

replace.rationale: Status is persisted and retrievable via the CHO backend; a FHIR PAS $inquire operation is not implemented.

qnxt.rationale: QNXT status inquiry is per-engagement integration work.
QNXT-sourced denial reasons are per-engagement integration work.

replace.rationale: A pended decision signals outstanding review (X12 A4); a full CDex request/response round-trip is not implemented.

scenarios.name: Drug exclusion from medical PA scope

replace.rationale: The CHO Replace-mode authorization workflow enforces benefit drug/service exclusions: a request for a plan-excluded drug (or the pharmacy service type, out of the CMS-0057-F medical scope) is recorded as a coded denial and persisted with audit history, rather than following the ordinary approvable path.

scenarios.name: Provider Access — attributed member data pull

qnxt.rationale: QNXT provider directory pull is per-engagement integration work; product path uses the CHO projection.

replace.rationale: Payer-to-Payer is out of scope at the FHIR adapter layer; no inbound respond surface yet.
No enrollment/opt-in-triggered outbound initiation or ingestion target.
Opt-in is modeled as an Active consent; no dedicated Payer-to-Payer ConsentType yet.
No $member-match / concurrent-coverage surface in product code.

scenarios.name: Patient Access — member claims / CARIN EOB

qnxt.rationale: QNXT claims read is per-engagement integration work; product path projects CHO claims to CARIN EOB.

replace.rationale: Demographics validate against US Core; broader USCDI clinical data lives in an external clinical store.
PA data is a recognized resource type; the >=1-year retention / 1-business-day freshness job is not implemented.
SMART discovery, scopes, and PKCE are served; the identity provider is configured per engagement.
One registry carries the opt-in/opt-out lifecycle; no dedicated Provider-Access/P2P ConsentType yet.

qnxt.rationale: Metrics over QNXT-owned authorization data are per-engagement integration work; product path derives from the persisted CHO authorization record. The full public-metrics extract job remains engagement work.
